# CO₂ monitoring in schools

URL: https://iot-fabrikken.com/en/library/co2-monitoring-in-schools/
Description: Measure CO₂ in classrooms and teaching spaces and document the indoor climate. Better air means more focused students — and compliance with BR18 and workplace-environment requirements.
Category: indoor-climate
Tags: module:indoor-climate", industry:schools", sensor:co2", standard:br18", standard:en-16798", type:guide", level:beginner"
Updated: 2026-04-22

Poor indoor climate is one of the biggest invisible drags on schools. When CO₂ rises above 1,200 ppm, students' ability to focus drops noticeably — and above 2,000 ppm, both headaches and fatigue start to set in. At the same time, CO₂ is one of the easiest parameters to measure, understand and act on.

## Measure every classroom — not just the building

With a single RoomAlyzer sensor per room you get a **precise, continuous picture** of air quality. Caretakers and management get:

- Alarms when CO₂ rises above your chosen thresholds during teaching hours.
- Monthly reports per classroom, per floor and per school.
- Comparisons across buildings in the municipality.
- Documentation that holds up to workplace inspections or questions from the student council.

## From measurement to action

Data alone doesn't change the air. That's why RoomAlyzer can pass CO₂ data on to your ventilation system via [MQTT](/en/library/mqtt-integration/), so ventilation ramps up precisely where it's needed — and back down when the room is empty.

This gives you the best of both worlds: better indoor climate for students **and** lower energy consumption.

## Typical setup for a school

1. One MINI+ sensor per classroom (up to 10 years of battery life).
2. One Full sensor in a few reference rooms (also gives VOC and sound levels).
3. A single gateway per building — or pure NB-IoT if the municipality prefers it.
4. Platform access for caretakers, management and, where relevant, a facilities advisor.

We handle the whole setup for you and help you set the thresholds, so you don't drown in alarms.

# Humidity in churches

URL: https://iot-fabrikken.com/en/library/humidity-in-churches/
Description: Monitor humidity in churches with wireless sensors. Protect organs, altarpieces and historic furnishings from mould, rot and drying out — and document the effort for your diocese and authorities.
Category: preservation
Tags: module:preservation, industry:churches, sensor:humidity, sensor:temperature, standard:en-15757, type:guide, level:intermediate
Updated: 2026-04-22

If you work with building preservation in churches — or are part of the daily operations — you know how important it is to protect these buildings and their furnishings. Churches are not just rooms for faith and tradition. They are often filled with priceless cultural heritage: historic organs, wall paintings, wood carvings, antique furniture and manuscripts that must be preserved for future generations.

Many of these materials are especially sensitive to changes in humidity. **Too much moisture** can lead to mould, rot and corrosion — especially on organ pipes, altarpieces and pews. **Air that is too dry** can cause cracks in wood, dry out adhesives and damage old documents. The damage often occurs slowly and invisibly, but by the time it's discovered it is expensive and time-consuming to repair — and in the worst case irreversible.

That is why it is essential to be able to follow humidity levels **continuously** and act in time.

## Get a full overview — locally and centrally

As a verger, priest, advisor or buildings officer in a diocese, you carry the responsibility for good conditions in the church's rooms and buildings. With RoomAlyzer you can monitor humidity in every part of the church — from the sacristy to the organ loft, the roof space and the crypt.

You get:

- Warnings in time if the climate moves outside your desired limits.
- Clear graphs and reports that document the measurements over time.
- A single view across multiple churches if you sit at the diocese.
- App access for vergers and priests — act from your phone.

It makes it easy to prioritise inspections, maintenance and interventions **before damage occurs**.

## Easy installation — flexible solutions with long battery life

**RoomAlyzer MINI+** is our most popular sensor for churches and historic buildings. It measures both temperature and relative humidity with high accuracy and includes an algorithm that automatically assesses the risk of mould growth.

- Sends readings about every two hours over the mobile network (NB-IoT).
- Up to 10 years of battery life.
- Requires no WiFi, cabling or gateway.
- Installed discreetly with a small screw or an adhesive pad — and can be moved as needed.

If you need near-real-time data in particularly sensitive rooms, MINI+ can be supplemented with **RoomAlyzer HUMIDITY**. The combination gives you both broad coverage and fast reaction times.

You get intuitive graphs, user-friendly reports and notifications via SMS or email when something requires action. We take care of the whole setup — both hardware and software — and help you get started smoothly.

## Concrete scenarios we cover

- **Organ lofts** — tight monitoring of humidity and temperature that protects pipes, wood and leather bellows.
- **Chancels and altarpieces** — alarms if humidity approaches mould thresholds.
- **Roof spaces and loft construction** — early warnings of condensation and leaks.
- **Crypts and basements** — continuous monitoring in rooms that are rarely visited.
- **Diocesan overview** — a single view of every church, prioritised by risk.

> "Previously, we had no objective knowledge of the humidity in our oldest churches. Now we see exactly when to act — and it saves both worry and money."
>
> — Buildings officer, Danish diocese

## Want to know more?

We have extensive experience measuring [indoor climate](/en/modules/indoor-climate/) and preservation climates in churches, museums and archives across Europe. Whether you are responsible for a single building or an entire diocese with hundreds of churches, we're ready to deliver quickly and effectively.

Reach out — and we'll take a no-strings chat about your situation.

# Leak sensors for basements and plant rooms

URL: https://iot-fabrikken.com/en/library/leak-sensors-for-basements-and-plant-rooms/
Description: Basements and plant rooms are where water damage typically starts — and where it is discovered last. Wireless leak sensors alert you the moment it happens.
Category: water-detection
Tags: module:water-detection", industry:property-management", industry:housing-associations", sensor:water-detector", type:niche", level:intermediate"
Updated: 2026-04-22

Basements and plant rooms are the most exposed spaces in a building — and at the same time the worst monitored. Most are only visited by a caretaker once a month, and as a result a developing leak is rarely spotted before it has done real damage.

## Typical water sources in plant rooms

- **Water heaters** that suddenly spring a leak after 12–15 years of service.
- **Circulation pumps** that drip from axle seals.
- **Pipe joints** in the main installation — especially near floor penetrations.
- **Drain covers and floor drains** that clog up and cause backup.
- **Air-conditioning and heat exchangers** that condense during warm periods.

## Put sensors where you *don't* want water

We typically recommend 4–8 sensors per plant room:

1. One directly under the water heater.
2. One at the base of the circulation pump.
3. One next to the main inlet stopcock.
4. One at each pipe joint by a floor penetration.
5. One by the drain cover in the floor.
6. One extra near the entrance — for back-flow situations.

Every sensor documents itself on a [floor plan](/en/library/water-detection-stop-damage-before-it-spreads/) in the platform, so new caretakers and technicians can get oriented quickly.

## What do customers use it for?

- **Housing associations** — one sensor per stairwell in the basement, alarms go to the caretaker and a committee mobile.
- **Municipal properties** — a standard pack per school and daycare, integrated with the operations centre.
- **Holiday homes and empty premises** — monitoring of rooms without regular supervision.
- **Hospitals and laboratories** — at critical installations, where downtime is expensive.

Want help planning sensor placement for your basement? Book a demo — we're happy to come and look at the conditions.

# MQTT integration

URL: https://iot-fabrikken.com/en/library/mqtt-integration/
Description: Stream real-time data from every RoomAlyzer sensor into your own systems via MQTT. Set roles, topics and access — and get data straight into BMS, BI tools or data platforms.
Category: integrations
Tags: module:platform", sensor:gateway", type:integration", type:technical", level:advanced"
Updated: 2026-04-22

MQTT is the most widely used protocol for sending IoT data between systems. It is lightweight, real-time, and supported by every major BMS, SCADA and data-warehouse platform. That's why it is our preferred route when customers want **RoomAlyzer data directly in their own systems**.

## How it works

1. You get a TLS endpoint, a username and a certificate from us.
2. You subscribe to the topics you care about — or the whole tree.
3. Your system receives a message each time a sensor reports in.

No polling, no lag, and no bespoke development.

## What do customers use it for?

- Push CO₂ and presence data into BMS to run ventilation on demand.
- Stream indoor-climate data into Power BI or Tableau for ESG reporting.
- Trigger tickets in ServiceNow or TOPdesk when a sensor goes into alarm.
- Feed ML models with historic and real-time data on the same channel.

## Typical payload

```json
{
  "time": "2026-04-22T08:14:31Z",
  "tenant": "municipality-x",
  "building": "north-school",
  "device": "class-2a-sensor",
  "type": "co2",
  "value": 847,
  "unit": "ppm"
}
```

See the full specification in our [OpenAPI documentation](/en/library/mqtt-integration/#api) (link coming — contact us for access).

# Water alarms in server rooms and IT infrastructure

URL: https://iot-fabrikken.com/en/library/water-alarms-in-server-rooms/
Description: A single drip on the wrong rack can cost a whole business day. Place wireless sensors under raised floors and next to cooling units, and get an alarm the instant moisture is detected.
Category: water-detection
Tags: module:water-detection", industry:data-centres", industry:it", sensor:water-detector", type:niche", level:advanced", Uptime"
Updated: 2026-04-22

A CRAC unit that dumps condensate onto the floor of a server room is rarely a matter of *if* — it's a matter of *when*. And when it happens at 3 a.m. on a Saturday, response time is the single most important thing you've got.

## What the CRAC unit's own sensors miss

Most server rooms have one sensor built into the CRAC unit. It covers **the unit's own drip tray**. It doesn't catch:

- Condensation on overhead pipes.
- Leaks from fire valves and sprinkler installations.
- Water that gets in from outside via floor penetrations.
- A leak in a UPS cooling loop.
- A thaw that hits a rooftop server room.

That's why we always recommend a dedicated detection solution **on top of** whatever the equipment itself provides.

## Typical sensor plan

For a medium-sized server room (10–20 racks):

1. One sensor under each CRAC unit.
2. One sensor per row under the raised floor.
3. One sensor by the door and at pipe penetrations.
4. One sensor under UPS battery cabinets.
5. One sensor at a low point where water pools if anything slips in.

Every sensor is shown on a floor plan, so NOC staff can see **exactly** where the alarm is triggered — not just "there's water in the server room".

## Integration patterns we see

- **ServiceNow / Jira / TOPdesk** — automatic P1 ticket when an alarm is triggered.
- **[MQTT to the NOC](/en/library/mqtt-integration/)** — real-time data into your existing monitoring.
- **Phone tree** — if the on-call person doesn't acknowledge within X minutes, the next one is called.
- **Email to the insurance broker** — to document the response time in the event of a claim.

## What does downtime cost?

Our customers in the data-centre segment have told us that even five minutes of extra response time easily costs a six-figure sum in SLA refunds. Seen in that light, the investment in dedicated water detection is negligible.

# Water-damage insurance — documentation with sensors

URL: https://iot-fabrikken.com/en/library/water-damage-insurance-documentation/
Description: IoT sensors unlock insurance discounts, faster claims settlement and full documentation of when a leak was detected and when it was acted on. Several insurers already offer a discount.
Category: water-detection
Tags: module:water-detection", industry:property-management", industry:insurance", sensor:water-detector", type:business-case", level:intermediate"
Updated: 2026-04-22

Insurers have got smarter — and they reward customers who actively reduce the risk of big water-damage claims. For a property portfolio, the premium discount can easily cover the whole investment in sensors, before you even count the value of the damage you avoid.

## The three things the insurer typically wants to see

1. **A sensor plan** — where the sensors are placed and what they cover.
2. **Response time** — how quickly an alarm reaches the on-call person.
3. **Event log** — an audit trail with test alarms and real events.

All of this is produced automatically by the platform, so you don't have to compile it manually.

## What happens when things do go wrong?

Water detection **isn't** about avoiding every claim — some leaks are unavoidable. But the time stamps from the sensors make a huge difference when the claim is assessed:

- **When did the leak start?** — the sensor has the first detection.
- **When did someone act?** — the escalation log shows who got the alarm and when they acknowledged.
- **How big is the damage?** — the sensor shows how long water has been running.

That means **faster claim settlement**, less debate about the deductible and typically a smaller claim overall — because action was taken quickly.

## Typical business case

For a housing association with 120 flats and a shared basement that we've worked with:

- **Investment**: around DKK 30,000 for 40 sensors and the platform over 3 years.
- **Premium discount**: 12 % of the water-damage insurance — about DKK 18,000 per year.
- **Avoided damage, year one**: a detected leak under a washing machine on the first floor, stopped after 4 minutes. The loss adjuster assessed the avoided damage at DKK 180,000.

On top of that comes the peace of mind of knowing that no leak is allowed to develop unnoticed for weeks.

Want to know what your current insurance offers? [Contact us](/en/contact/) — we're happy to help with the conversation to your broker.

# Water detection — stop damage before it spreads

URL: https://iot-fabrikken.com/en/library/water-detection-stop-damage-before-it-spreads/
Description: Wireless water sensors that alarm via SMS/email within seconds, so a small leak never turns into a large water-damage claim. Full overview across buildings and sites.
Category: water-detection
Tags: module:water-detection", industry:property-management", industry:offices", sensor:water-detector", type:guide", level:beginner"
Updated: 2026-04-22

A water-damage claim rarely starts with a bang. It starts as a drop per second behind a pipe casing — and is only discovered when water is standing in the basement or the paint starts to bubble on the wall upstairs. By that point you are no longer talking about a repair, but a renovation.

That's why water detection isn't about **whether** water shows up, but about **how quickly you find out**.

## From drop to alarm in under 60 seconds

RoomAlyzer's water detectors are small, wireless units that sit low on the floor or are fixed in wet zones. The moment water touches the sensor:

1. The sensor sends a message into the platform.
2. The platform matches the alarm against your escalation rules.
3. The on-call person gets SMS and email — and a backup person is contacted if no one acknowledges.

The whole sequence typically takes under a minute, whether it's 2 p.m. on a Tuesday or 3 a.m. on Christmas Eve.

## Where should we put them?

Typical placements at our customers:

- Under washing machines, dishwashers and fridges with water connections.
- By [water heaters and plant equipment](/en/library/leak-sensors-for-basements-and-plant-rooms/) in basements.
- At pipe penetrations between floors.
- Under raised floors in [server rooms and data centres](/en/library/water-alarms-in-server-rooms/).
- In museum stores, archives and depots, where a leak can ruin irreplaceable assets.
- In empty holiday homes and second residences without regular supervision.

## What you get out of the box

- **Dashboard** with status for every sensor across buildings.
- **Floor-plan view** so you can see exactly where an alarm was triggered.
- **Escalation rules** that you control yourself — roles, time windows and backup contacts.
- **Logbook** with every event, acknowledgement and resolution — ready for the insurer.

Want a concrete proposal for sensor placement in your building? Book a demo, and we'll walk through it together.
